text:
Rhea: I put together a short checklist of control-plane invariants we should *really* keep strongly consistent across regions before we publish an RFC: leases (whois primary), routing rules (policy changes), and tenant residency tags. Diagram in drive: https://redwood/internal/drive/multisite/controlplane-checklist.png
Tom: Agree. If leases are eventually consistent we're going to see split-primary writes. Strong lease semantics are a must. Can we keep lease authority per-tenant pinned to a single control-plane leader with async readers?
Ibrahim: Thats the model I prefer: single-writer per-tenant (leader election) with a lease token. Readers can cache for short TTL but must validate on write path. Proto sketch:
```
service LeaseService {
  rpc Acquire(LeaseRequest) returns (LeaseResponse);
}
message LeaseRequest { string tenant_id = 1; string preferred_site = 2; int64 ttl_ms = 3; string idempotency_key = 4; }
message LeaseResponse { string holder_site = 1; int64 expires_at_ms = 2; string lease_token = 3; }
```
Priya: Note: for residency-locked tenants the lease must be awarded only to a site inside the allowed region set. If request tries to acquire elsewhere return 451+info header. That prevents accidental cross-border primaries.
Rhea: Good call. Also callout for KMS: key material for residency tenants must never be exported. We need a site-local KMS policy and proof-of-possession header on RPCs that wrote payload to local storage.
Tom: Data-plane warmup: model weights and KV caches. Idea: maintain a per-site prefetch queue for top-N models and prefixes. Prefetch controller should respect residency flags (no raw prefetch for locked tenants). Use a lightweight consent stamp instead: {tenant, hash(prefix), consent=false}.
Ibrahim: Observability: add span attribute `site.hint` and `tenant.residency`. Also metric `routing.control_plane_handoff{tenant,from_site,to_site,reason}`. Keep label cardinality low by sampling low-volume tenants.
Priya: Operator preflight: before any node-level cutover/upgrade run check: (1) no tenant migrations in past 15m, (2) KMS sync ok, (3) prefetch queue drained for models >90th percentile traffic. If any fail, abort. ops-bot should implement.
Tom: Conflict reconciliation appendix: for writes that may be produced during a transient dual-primary, we classify data types: inference_input=retry-idempotent (client-provided request_id), model_metadata=merge-CRDT, billing=append-only with dedupe by event-id.
Rhea: Testing matrix (short): 1) leader-loss: kill control-plane leader for N tenants and assert no split-primary. 2) cross-site overload: push traffic to cause preemption and verify residency tenants receive 429+route-hint, others failover. 3) KMS blackout: ensure residency writes fail-safe.
ops-bot: [policy] preflight rule created: `no_migrations_last_15m` with blocking severity.
